title: The Secret Claude Code Command You're not Using (/loop)
description:
Claude Code /loop command explained, run one prompt on a repeating interval for up to 72 hours, and it actually remembers each cycle.

You can type /loop, give it one prompt and a time interval, like every 10 minutes, and Claude wakes up, runs that exact prompt, checks the result, then goes back to standby until the next cycle. Unlike a plain cron job, /loop keeps context between wake-ups, so it can build on what happened in the previous cycle instead of running blind each time. It can stay active for up to 72 hours, good for things like monitoring a deployment, polling for a status change, or repeated review passes, not really built for lightweight one-off tasks.

In this video:
→ How to start a loop with /loop and a real interval
→ Why it's different from a cron job
→ What kinds of tasks it's actually built for
→ A real live demo showing multiple completed cycles
